column4: God assigns Abraham the site of the House, commands no association, and tells him to purify it for circling, standing, bowing, and prostration. It supplies the worshipful home at the road’s end.
Pilgrims complete their rites and circumambulate the Ancient House. Its own contribution is the final arrival and circling that follows the sacrifice passage.
Honoring God’s symbols is said to arise from piety of hearts. It explains why the animals in the neighboring rites are signs rather than ends in themselves.
Completing pilgrimage includes an available sacrifice, and the offering must reach its place before a head is shaved. It joins completion, animal, and destination at the House.
Moses answers Pharaoh that the true Lord is Lord of the heavens, earth, and what lies between them. It replaces Pharaoh’s claimed nurture with cosmic Rabbhood.
Moses further names the Lord of east, west, and what lies between them. The verse turns the dispute over possession into orientation under the real Lord.
God directs the infant Moses through the river and says He cast love upon him so that he would be brought up under God’s care. It is true nurture beneath Pharaoh’s household.
Moses is returned to his mother so her eye may be comforted, then saved and tested. It completes the divine care that contrasts with Pharaoh’s later boast of raising him.
Moses leaves the city fearful and asks his Lord to save him from the wrongdoing people. It supplies the flight that immediately precedes his request for a level way.
Moses is offered eight years of service, with completion of ten left to him. It makes service and a chosen completion-limit part of the Midian journey’s own outcome.
Moses’ thirty-night appointment is completed with ten, so his Lord’s term becomes forty nights. It gives the section’s completion-at-a-boundary image a Moses-and-Rabb form.
People are commanded to worship their Rabb, who created them and those before them. It grounds worship in the Creator-nurturer rather than in an unknown master.
The same Rabb makes earth a resting place, sky a canopy, and rain a source of fruit provision. Ground, water, plant, and dependence form one worship scene.
God makes earth a cradle and lays paths through it so people may be guided. It directly joins formed ground, road, and guidance.
God sends water from the sky in due measure and revives dead land. It adds measured rain and renewal to the section’s water-and-measure meeting.
God creates pairs and makes ships and livestock for riding. It joins formed creatures, travel, and animal mounts in the same divine ordering.
When people settle on the backs of those mounts, they remember God’s favor and glorify the one who subjected them. The road-rider answers with praise for subjection.
God knows what every womb bears and each decrease or increase within it; everything has a measure with Him. It precisely joins womb, hidden growth, and measure.
God brings people from their mothers’ wombs knowing nothing, then gives hearing, sight, and hearts for gratitude. It gives nurture a path from hidden formation to response.
The human being is asked what deceived them about their generous Rabb. It makes the section’s true Lord a question of recognition before the Day of Recompense.
The Rabb creates, forms, and balances the human being. Formation and upright proportion meet before the passage turns to reckoning.
God composes the human in whatever form He wills. It contributes the deliberate shaping behind the section’s womb-and-sign imagery.
The passage immediately says people deny the Day of Recompense. It binds formed humanity to the dīn-day named in the section.
God is addressed as owner of sovereignty, giving and taking rule, honoring and humbling. It unfolds the section’s Malik image as active possession and reversal.
Blessed is the one in whose hand is all dominion. It gives the section’s kingly hand a direct Qur’anic statement of universal ownership.
All things’ dominion is in God’s hand, and to Him people return. Ownership here includes the homeward return imagined at the road’s end.
Moses says he hastened to his Lord so that He might be pleased. This is the immediate positive counterpart to the anger-and-guidance sequence of 20:81–82.
The tranquil soul appears at the end of judgment. It gives the favorable side of the Day an inward condition before its return.
The soul is told to return to its Lord, pleased and pleasing. Divine pleasure, response, and return to the Rabb converge explicitly.
The returned soul is told to enter among God’s servants. Its own contribution is the fulfilled belonging of the willing servant.
The final command is to enter God’s Paradise. It supplies a home beyond the road for the returning, pleased soul.
On the Day some faces are whitened and some blackened; the blackened faces are confronted with punishment. It gives the section’s two judgment-faces a sharp visual division.
Those whose faces are whitened remain in God’s mercy. It supplies the favorable face’s lasting relation to divine mercy.
Those who do good receive the best and more, and neither dust nor humiliation covers their faces. It directly answers the section’s dust-covered Day-face.
The final garden reward culminates in God being pleased with them and they with Him. It gives rıza its mutual, eschatological completion.
Gardens and lasting dwellings are followed by the declaration that God’s pleasure is greater. It distinguishes the giver’s pleasure from the gifts of the final home.
The command to give full measure and weigh with the upright balance uses the language of straightness. It makes the section’s scale and straight road share an ethical posture.
Shuʿayb commands worship of the one God, full measure and weight, and no defrauding. Worship and an unbent balance are one public way.
Shuʿayb calls his people to worship God alone and not diminish measure or weight. The verse joins the true master to the exact fraud scene.
He commands full measure and just weight and warns of an encompassing Day’s punishment. It binds market balance directly to the Day of account.
“Give full measure” and do not be among those who cause loss. It names the receiving side of the scale that the section makes answerable to judgment.
“Weigh with the straight balance” makes the section’s uprightness literal in commercial measurement.
Do not deprive people of their due or spread corruption in the land. It gives the imbalance a social consequence beyond the instrument itself.
Abraham asks forgiveness for believers on the Day when the account will stand. It joins Abraham, standing, and the section’s Day of debt-accounting.
David must judge with truth and not follow desire lest it lead him from God’s way; the warning is punishment on the Day of Account. Judgment, path, and reckoning meet.
Moses is commanded to make a dry path through the sea for the Children of Israel. It gives water-and-road a direct Exodus form.
Moses strikes the sea and it splits into towering parts. It supplies the water that becomes passable space for the guided people.
God sends winds as mercy and sends down purifying water from the sky. It gives the section’s cloud-water provision a merciful source.
That water revives dead land and gives drink to livestock and many people. It explicitly distributes the provision to herd and traveller together.
Water is driven to barren land, producing crops eaten by livestock and people. It repeats the section’s pasture-provision meeting in a land made alive.
Water is poured down abundantly. It begins a compact provision sequence in which rainfall is the source of the ground’s gifts.
The earth is split open. It gives the received water a shaped, opening ground rather than an undifferentiated field.
Grain is grown from that opened earth. It supplies a staple of the nourishment that follows water and formation.
Fruit and pasture appear together. The verse directly reunites human provision with the herd’s grazing ground.
The produce is enjoyment for people and their livestock. It states the shared provision that the section’s route and herd imply.
Every living creature is created from water, with distinct ways of moving. It links water, formed creatures, and the animal movement beneath the section’s road imagery.
God guides whom He wills to a straight path. Its own contribution is the guidance that follows the water-created creatures of 24:45.
God calls to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path. It names both the destination-house and the road toward it.
Satan vows to sit in wait on God’s straight path. It gives the section’s journey an active obstructer rather than only an abstract crooked way.
Satan says he will approach people from before, behind, right, and left to make them ungrateful. It fills out how the obstruction around the straight path operates.
God says, “This is a straight path to Me.” It makes the straight road’s endpoint the Lord Himself.
Satan has no authority over God’s servants except those who follow him among the astray. It marks the boundary between owned servants and the lost followers.
The Qur’an guides to what is most upright. Its أَقْوَم language links the debt verse’s upright testimony to the section’s upright road.
The Prophet is declared to be upon a straight path. It gives the section’s leading guide a messenger who himself stands on the route.
People are told that their God is one, so direct themselves uprightly to Him and seek forgiveness. It joins monotheistic ownership, uprightness, and return.
After descent, God promises guidance; whoever follows it will neither go astray nor suffer. It supplies a direct answer to the section’s fear of becoming lost.
When guidance comes, those who follow it have no fear and do not grieve. It makes following the given road the opposite of exposed strayness.
People who went astray, led many astray, and wandered from the even way are named as a warning. It gives the section’s lost herd a human, imitated path of deviation.
One party is guided while another merits error because it took devils as protectors instead of God. False patronage becomes the mechanism of thinking oneself guided while lost.
Hūd says his Lord is upon a straight path. The true Rabb is not merely beside the road but the reliable order by which it is straight.
Land creatures and birds are communities like people, and all are gathered to their Lord. It gives the herd its own communal relation to the known Rabb and final gathering.
Sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, animals, and many people prostrate to God. Celestial signs, herd, and worship are gathered under the Creator rather than worshipping one another.
Livestock contain a lesson: people drink from them, receive benefits, and eat. It gives the section’s herd its provision and instruction together.
People are carried on livestock and ships. It extends the animal from provision into the traveller’s means of passage.
A creditor must defer a debtor in hardship, and remission is better. It supplies the merciful human relation that the debt-accounting passage leaves at stake.
Believers are commanded to stand firmly for justice even against themselves or relatives. It gives the section’s standing balance an embodied witness.
Believers are commanded to stand firmly for God as witnesses with justice, without hatred bending them. It turns uprightness into a refusal to tilt judgment.
Abraham settles descendants near the Sacred House, asks that hearts incline toward it, and asks for fruit provision. House, directed longing, and sustenance meet in his prayer.
Moses seeks refuge in his Lord from every arrogant person who does not believe in the Day of Account. It connects his true Rabb to the very accounting Pharaoh’s rule denies.
God’s parable asks whether people would accept their slaves as equal partners in their own provision. It clarifies why creatures cannot be co-owners with the one true master.
